Caveat for the curator: several African series have a step artefact at 1996 or 2002-03 where the source switches to an agglomeration definition (Lagos 1999:1.4M -> 2000:8.7M, Kano 1995:657k -> 1996:2.9M, Cairo 2002:7.8M -> 2003:19.1M), so some of the visible growth in that decade is a definition change, not people.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: 'Year of Africa' is a real term but it is a journalism label rather than an event. Replaced with the countable fact under it - 17 states in 1960. Deliberately not pinned to one independence (Nigeria, 1 Oct 1960, would have matched the Lagos anchor) because the note is carrying the whole continent.

Coordinate and number both from the data: Brasília's curve begins at 1960:140k and there is nothing there before, so the bubble appears out of blank cerrado exactly when the note fires - one of the cleanest positive counterparts to Vijayanagara on the map. It then goes 1969:498k > 1979:1.1M > 2025:2.4M. The 2000:2.0M > 2001:1.4M step is a definition change, not a loss; the note sits well clear of it.

Berlin. cities.json: 4.3M(1940), 3.2M(1946), 3.3M(1959), 3.3M(1963), 3.3M(1986), 3.5M(1991) - forty years dead flat while Hamburg goes 1.4M to 2.2M and Frankfurt 424k to 1.4M. West Berlin actually shrank (about 2.2M to 2.0M) and East Berlin grew; the flat line is the two netting out. im -1 is really 'stops' rather than 'declines' - there is no zero-growth colour on the scale and im 0 would wrongly promise something is coming. Two definition steps to watch here and not mistake for reunification: 1991:3.5M to 1993:4.0M, and 2000:3.4M to 2001:4.2M. The earlier 1919:1.9M to 1925:4.0M step is the 1920 Greater Berlin Act, a pure boundary change.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: the bare name did not say which way - up or down - and the note is 1961 with im:-1. The d is the same fact as the deleted '3.3M in 1946, still 3.3M in 1989' with one number instead of four.

Dhaka 23.8041/90.4152: 1968:873k, 1973:1.6M, 1980:3.2M, 1988:5.0M, 2001:9.9M, 2025:37.6M. The war's mortality (300k-3M, bitterly disputed) and the ten million refugees into India leave no dip anywhere - the city only climbs - so the note is marked +3 and describes what the map shows, with the war in the detail line. Watch the 2001-to-2002 step from 9.9M to 19.3M: that is a switch from city to agglomeration, not growth. Seed for the whole post-1970 megacity set - Karachi, Jakarta (1969:4.2M to 2025:41.9M) and Manila 14.5995/120.9842 (1969:3.4M to 2025:27.4M) all do the same thing over the same fifty years and none of them has a note.

events.d: Riyadh, Kuwait and Dubai bring in foreign workers
events.p: Retitled and re-aimed at Anita's suggestion. The detail now names the actual demographic mechanism rather than the money: Gulf city growth from 1973 is overwhelmingly imported labour, not local birth rate, which is why these cities climb so much faster than their countries do. Riyadh, Kuwait and Dubai all bend at 1973. Pairs with the 1938 Dammam marker.

events.d: herders move into Nouakchott and Niamey
events.p: The 1968-74 drought is what turns the Sahel's colonial garrison towns into cities. Nouakchott, planted as a capital in 1958, is 1973:70k -> 1976:119k -> 1986:270k -> 1.6M today; Niamey 1969:70k -> 1976:203k; Ouagadougou 1970:117k -> 1979:234k; Bamako 1967:364k -> 1975:400k -> 4.8M. Anchored at Nouakchott because it is the most extreme and because it is on the desert edge where the herders actually came from. 1973 is the worst year of the drought.

events.t: Americans move to the Sun Belt
events.p:
Re-anchored from Phoenix to ATLANTA at Anita's request - it reads as the centre of the Sun Belt even though Phoenix and Houston are the cities that actually rise on this map. Atlanta's own curve is the trap: flat at 495k from 1969 to 1999, then 416k in 2000 and 4.4M in 2001, which is the metropolitan-definition switch and not growth. The detail line deliberately names no city, so the note is about the region and does not claim something Atlanta's bubble contradicts.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: YEAR MOVED 1973 -> 1979 to fire with the Rust Belt note, which is the other half of the same movement - Anita's call. 1979 is defensible on its own: US manufacturing employment peaks that year. Headline verbed off the bare region name. WATCH: Atlanta and Detroit are only ~1,000km apart, which is close at world zoom, so one may lose its slot - check_events.py will say. If it does, 1978/1980 still reads as a pair.

Anchored Detroit. Wants a growth counterpart on Phoenix/Houston/Atlanta.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: verbed off the bare region name and paired with the Sun Belt note, now also at 1979. The growth counterpart this note asked for is that pairing.

Renamed from 'Deng opens the coast', which was doing metaphor work. Shenzhen is the first of the four zones, declared August 1980; the county is 30k and reaches 14M by 2020. Its 2001-02 step is the administrative/built-up artefact this project flags for Chinese cities, so no claim is hung on that part of the curve.

Pripyat: 49,360 people, founded 1970, evacuated on 27 April 1986 in about three hours by 1,200 buses. It is not in cities.json at all - the nearest records are Chernihiv 86km and Kyjiv 111km - so this leader deliberately points at a blank piece of map, the same trick as the Columbus and Gulf oil notes. It will not trip the 400km warning because Chernihiv is inside that radius. The 350,000 is the cumulative resettlement out of the 30km zone plus the later Belarusian and Ukrainian relocations, not the April 1986 evacuation alone. im -3 because the zone is permanent: Pripyat is the one 20th-century European city that is simply gone.

Murmansk, the largest city inside the Arctic Circle. An im 0 marker is literally what the curve does here: cities.json holds Murmansk flat at 468k from 1990 to 2000 and only then drops it - 371k(2001), 322k(2010), 292k(2025). Vorkuta 116k(1990) to 55k(2000), Magadan 153k to 77k(2025); Norilsk is not in the data. The mechanism is the end of the northern wage coefficients and the unwinding of the Gulag-descended mining towns, not war. The Baltic half is real but mixed - Riga 903k(1988) to 769k(2025), while Tallinn and Vilnius grow - so d claims only the Arctic. Riga's 2001:908k to 2002:747k step is a definition change, not emigration.

events.d: factory towns grow along the border
events.p:
Anchored Ciudad Juárez (31.6904/-106.4245). The border cities were already growing on the 1965 Border Industrialization Program - Juárez 1940:78k > 1989:773k - but there is a real NAFTA-era inflection: 1979:610k > 1989:773k is 27% in a decade, 1989:773k > 2000:1.2M is 55% in eleven years. Tijuana (32.5332/-117.0193) runs in parallel, 1989:724k > 2000:1.2M, and Mexicali is the third. Both cross a million in the late 1990s, so 'pass a million' is a forward-looking statement from 1994 rather than a 1994 fact - same construction as the existing Gulf oil note.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: 'Maquiladoras on the border' reads as journalism and assumes the word. The datable event at this year is NAFTA, 1 Jan 1994. Honest caveat unchanged: the border was already growing on the 1965 Border Industrialization Program, and NAFTA is the inflection rather than the start. Dropping the old d also drops the forward-looking 'pass a million', which was the weakest thing in the note.

Re-aimed from Goma to KIGALI so the note is the genocide itself, as Anita asked. Kigali shows no drop at all (1990:246k -> 1997:330k), hence im 0; the visible movement is the refugee influx at Goma and Bukavu, which the detail line carries.

Baghdad keeps growing straight through (2000:3.8M -> 2005:5.2M, though the 2001 step is the metropolitan switch). im 0. Note the same city's 1258 note already carries a warning about its medieval curve.

The cleanest single-event bubble drop in the modern Americas and the one thing on this half of the map a viewer will definitely stop and ask about: 2005:1.3M > 2006:988k, a 24% fall in twelve months. 'A quarter' is the metropolitan figure the map draws; the city proper fell further, roughly 455k to 230k. im -2 rather than -3 because the curve does recover - 2007:1.1M > 2015:1.3M. Two things for the curator: the city proper never got back above about 85% of its 2000 level, and the second drop at 2019:1.3M > 2020:1.0M > 2022:976k looks like a metro-area redelineation rather than a second exodus, so nothing should be pinned to it.

Halab 36.2021/37.1343. The battle for Aleppo runs July 2012 to December 2016 and the map does move: 2010:8.0M -> 2015:2.4M -> 2020:5.2M -> 2025:6.2M. Caveat for the curator - the 8.0M is a metro/governorate figure (the city itself was about 2.1M in 2010), so the absolute numbers are wrong but the ~70% drop and the partial refill are the right shape, which is why the detail says 'most of it' and no number. Marked -2, not -3: it is coming back. Rejected: the Iran-Iraq war, because the data flatly contradicts it - Khorramshahr (30.4256/48.1891) is 1975:140k, 1985:150k, 2001:150k and Abadan (30.3666/48.2755) is flat at 300k from 1971 to 2001, when both were in fact evacuated and flattened; Basrah rises straight through the war (1987:406k, 1988:557k). A note there would have contradicted the bubbles under it.

VOICE PASS 2026-08-22: 'splits in two' did not say what had happened or that there was a war. The war is now named; the d says what the bubble does. 'Most of the city leaves' still carries no number, which is deliberate - the 8.0M is a metro/governorate figure and the absolute numbers are wrong even though the shape is right.

R4V counted about 4.5 million by end-2019, so 'four million' is safe at this pin; by 2024 it is nearly eight. Caracas is the rare Latin American bubble that shrinks: 2015:3.6M > 2020:3.1M > 2025:3.0M. The receiving curves are all still climbing - Bogotá 2020:10.2M > 2025:10.9M, Lima 2020:10.4M > 2025:11.0M, Santiago 2020:7.5M > 2025:7.7M - so the note works in both directions on the map. im -2 because the curve flattens rather than collapses and Venezuela is expected to refill.
Last event on the timeline. Data behind it is thin - WUP 2025 projections.
